chapters.heading: **1. BOCOUTURE® doesn't make my patients look as ‘wrinkle free’ as others toxins.**

content.text: **BOCOUTURE® has over 15 years of scientific and clinical evidence,¹ as well as over 200 publications and over 10 million vials sold worldwide.²**

The clinical trials and other analyses over the years have explored patient-reported outcomes. For example, in a study by Kane and colleagues in 2015, **97.4% of patients were extremely satisfied, satisfied or slightly satisfied with treatment with BOCOUTURE®** one month after treatment and were over 90% throughout the study.³
And in a retrospective analysis of clinical practice from patient notes by Prager and colleagues, **96.3% of physicians were satisfied with BOCOUTURE® treatment.⁴**
**Patient and physician satisfaction levels with BOCOUTURE® were high and similar to Botox® in both studies.³,⁴**

Looking at the Azzalure SmPC, it outlines a **rate of eye lid ptosis of 1–10%,⁵** while for **BOCOUTURE® it is lower than 1%.⁶** Assuming this was done with an accurate injection technique, this indicates BOCOUTURE is associated with less diffusion.
**As such BOCOUTURE® depends on an even more accurate injection technique than you may use with other toxins,** to ensure you reach the motor neuron needed for therapeutic effect.
**Using this very precise injection technique can also give you more confidence and further improve patient satisfaction** due to the adverse events associated with technique and misplaced toxin.⁷

chapters.heading: **2. BOCOUTURE® is not as long lasting as other toxins**

content.text: **Longevity of the treatment effect** is a key feature of aesthetics treatments and is important to patients as **it impacts cost.**
Studies of BOCOUTURE® for the treatment of glabellar frown lines, have reported **high responder rates over time and long median duration of treatment effect.**¹,²
For example, Kane and colleagues reported **responder rates of 89.7% and 62.1% at Months 2 and 4** respectively, after treatment with 20 U BOCOUTURE®¹
In a study by Kerscher and colleagues, **a single 20 U treatment of BOCOUTURE® had a median duration of action of 177 days which is approximately 6 months**²
The BOTOX® SmPC suggests it lasts only 4 months in glabellar frown lines after a single injection and Azzalure® suggests only 5 months.³,⁴

**Background information:**
• In the Kane et al. study, clinical response was defined as an improvement of ≥1 point compared with baseline¹
• Kerscher and colleagues assessed treatment duration as the time between injection and the return to baseline severity (n=151)²

chapters.heading: 3. Purity does not matter to me

content.text: Your patients today care deeply about what is in the cosmetic products and treatments they undergo with an increasing desire for 'healthy' and 'clean' products, particularly among millennials¹
In fact, research also shows that 4 out of 5 patients would be influenced by the purity if given the choice.²

Merz Aesthetics developed BOCOUTURE® with XTRACT™ technology creating the first and only highly purified BTX-A free of complexing proteins, only containing the required therapeutic component.³ Accordingly BOCOUTURE® provides an opportunity to attract and retain patients by virtue of the purity demand from patients.

Above all, from a biological point of view the complexing proteins are removed as they have no therapeutic purpose but constitute an unnecessary foreign protein load.³ They can be recognized by the immune system and stimulate an immune response risking the generation of neutralizing antibodies and secondary treatment failure.⁴

With this in mind BOCOUTURE® should be the only neurotoxin choice considered from an ethical responsibility stand point. The pandemic has put more pressure on our immune systems which we do not want to add to, plus patients are starting younger which means they run more risk of building resistance.

items: Recent consumer research in beauty and personal care, showed that 72% of respondents said it was important to purchase healthy or clean products¹
We asked 4,000 patients, "How important is the purity of botulinum toxin products to you personally?" 4 out of 5 patients desire a purified toxin²

The manufacturing process of BOCOUTURE® involves several chromatographic steps to purify the neurotoxin from the complexing proteins while minimizing the risk of denaturing, degrading or losing biological activity of the neurotoxin³

The neurotoxin itself does not contain any molecular signatures recognized by dendritic cells which may stimulate an immune response while the complexing proteins do, and are therefore identified as adjuvants.³
Neutralizing antibodies can result in partial or complete treatment failure³,⁴

chapters.heading: 4. I do not care about room temperature storage as I keep all products in the fridge anyway

content.text: To **safeguard from any efficacy challenges** in the event of an electrical failure effecting the fridge, or indeed if a product is left outside the fridge for a period of time (e.g. in transition to the fridge or treatment room in a larger clinic), **it is very important to have a product that can be stored at room temperature.**

Additionally, with the increased awareness of carbon emissions, the fact that **storage of BOCOUTURE® contributes to 90% fewer greenhouse gases and has less packaging to dispose of compared with other neurotoxins¹** is a great benefit clinics can use to attract patients.
Also, no cold chain means there are **no limitations in terms of special delivery services needed** to consistently get BOCOUTURE into clinics in a timely manner.

chapters.heading: 5. I have recently switched and I am not getting good results

content.text: **BOCOUTURE® has over 15 years of scientific and clinical evidence**,¹ as well as **over 200 publications** and **over 10 million vials** sold worldwide.²

In a retrospective analysis of clinical practice from patient notes by Prager and colleagues, **96.3% of physicians were satisfied with BOCOUTURE® treatment**.³ However, even for the most experienced practitioners, we find a small amount of learning is needed for successful transition.
First **BOCOUTURE® requires very careful reconstitution** due to its dry-freeze powder form.⁴ There is a reconstitution animation I can show you to demonstrate the steps.

Second, BOCOUTURE® has shown lower diffusion rate compared to other toxin⁵. As such, an **even more accurate injection technique** is required to ensure the target site is reached for optimal therapeutic effect.

**Background information:**
• In the Prager study, the documentation period was from March to June 2011 and data from 1256 patients were included⁴
• In the Kerscher 2012 study comparing the spread of BOCOUTURE®, BOTOX® and Azzalure®, Azzalure® showed a higher rate of spread at 6 weeks and also at 6 months⁵.

**Key supporting assets:**
• BOCOUTURE HCP Brochure
• Reconstitution Animation

chapters.heading: **6. Toxins are all similar, so I look for something cheaper than BOCOUTURE®**

content.text: **Not all botulinum toxin formulations are the same and only head-to-head studies can properly compare the efficacy and safety of different products.**

**BOCOUTURE®** has been studied in head-to-head clinical trials across indications – glabellar frown lines, lateral periorbital lines (crow’s feet), horizontal forehead lines, blepharospasm and cervical dystonia – which **have shown that it has comparable efficacy to other botulinum toxin A formulations including equipotency to Botox® for the treatment of glabellar frown lines.**¹⁻⁵ **BOCOUTURE®** also has proven efficacy for post-stroke upper limb spasticity.⁶

**A key differentiator of BOCOUTURE® is that it is the first and only pure toxin formulation without complexing proteins.**⁷ Complexing proteins can be recognized by the immune system and stimulate an immune response risking the generation of **neutralizing antibodies leading to treatment failure.**⁸,⁹

Another benefit of **BOCOUTURE®** is the long median duration of action, which has been in a study by Kerscher and colleagues: a single 20 U treatment of **BOCOUTURE®** for glabellar lines had a **median duration of action of 177 days, which is approximately 6 months**¹⁰

**For your patient, long duration of action can offset any potential savings from a cheaper priced neurotoxin/treatment.** This, along with the risk of developing neutralizing antibodies and secondary treatment failure, maximises physician’s **potential of providing great patient satisfaction and retaining patients for a lifetime of treatment.**

**BOCOUTURE®**, 50 or 100 units, powder for solution for injection. **Active substance**: Botulinum toxin type A (150 kD), purified from Clostridium Botulinum cultures (Hall strain), free from complexing proteins. Prescription-only medicine! **Qualitative and quantitative composition**: One vial contains: 50 or 100 units of Botulinum toxin type A (150 kD), free from complexing proteins, human albumin, sucrose. Due to the differences in the potency assay, unit doses are not interchangeable with those for other Botulinum toxin type A preparations.

**Therapeutic indications**: For temporary improvement in the appearance of upper facial lines in adults below 65 years when the severity of these lines has an important psychological impact for the patient:

items: moderate to severe vertical lines between the eyebrows seen at maximum frown (glabellar frown lines) and/or
moderate to severe lateral periorbital lines seen at maximum smile (crow's feet lines) and/or
moderate to severe horizontal forehead lines seen at maximum contraction.

content.text: **Contraindications**: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients, generalised disorders of muscle activity (e.g. myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton syndrome), infection or inflammation at the proposed injection site. Should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary and not be used during breast-feeding. **Undesirable effects**: Undesirable effects usually occur within the first week after injection and are temporary in nature. They may be related to the active substance, the injection procedure, or both.

**Application-related**: Localised pain, inflammation, paraesthesia, hypoesthesia, tenderness, swelling, oedema, erythema, itching, localised infection, haematoma, bleeding and/or bruising may be associated with the injection. Needle-related pain and/or anxiety may result in vasovagal responses, including transient symptomatic hypotension, nausea, tinnitus, and syncope.

**Undesirable effects of the substance class Botulinum toxin type A**: Localised muscle weakness, blepharoptosis (possibly caused by the injection technique) are an expression of the pharmacological effect. **Toxin spread**: When treating other indications with Botulinum toxins, undesirable effects related to spread of toxin distant from the site of administration producing symptoms consistent with Botulinum toxin type A effects have been reported very rarely (excessive muscle weakness, dysphagia, and aspiration pneumonia with a fatal outcome in some cases). These cannot be completely ruled out with the use of BOCOUTURE®. **Hypersensitivity reactions**: Rare reports of serious and/or immediate hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, serum sickness, urticaria, soft tissue oedema, and dyspnoea, some of these reactions either following the administration of conventional Botulinum toxin type A complex alone or in combination with other agents known to cause similar reactions. The following undesirable effects were reported from clinical experience with BOCOUTURE®: **Very common** (≥1/10); **common** (≥1/100 to <1/10); **uncommon** (≥1/1,000 to <1/100). **Vertical lines between the eyebrows seen at maximum frown (Glabellar Frown Lines)**: **Common**: Headache, Mephisto sign (lateral elevation of eyebrows); **Uncommon**: Bronchitis, nasopharyngitis, influenza-like illness, insomnia, eyelid oedema, eyelid ptosis, blurred vision, pruritus, skin nodule, brow ptosis, muscle twitching, muscle spasm, facial asymmetry (brow asymmetry), injection site haematoma, injection site pain, (local) tenderness, fatigue, discomfort (heavy feeling of eyelid/eyebrow), haematoma. **Lateral periorbital lines seen at maximum smile (Crow's Feet Lines)**: **Common**: Eyelid oedema, dry eye, injection site haematoma. **Upper Facial Lines**: **Very common**: Headache; **Common**: Hypoaesthesia, injection site haematoma, injection site pain, injection site erythema, discomfort (heavy feeling of the frontal area), eyelid ptosis, dry eye, brow ptosis, facial asymmetry, Mephisto sign (lateral elevation of eyebrows), nausea.

**Post-marketing experience**: **Frequency not known**: Hypersensitivity reactions like swelling, oedema (also distant from the injection site), erythema, pruritus, rash (localised and generalised), breathlessness, muscle atrophy, flu-like symptoms.
